title: Factorisation of the tilted exponential
statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\bbr$, and let $t\in\bbr$. Writing $\Lambda(t)$ for the cumulant generating function of $X$ under $\mu$ at $t$, the functions $x\mapsto e^{tX(x)-\Lambda(t)}$ and $x\mapsto e^{-\Lambda(t)}e^{tX(x)}$ are equal.
replaced:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $X\colon \Omega \to \bbr$,
and let $t \in \bbr$. Writing $\Lambda(t)$ for the cumulant generating function of $X$
under $\mu$ at $t$, the functions $x \mapsto e^{\,t X(x) - \Lambda(t)}$ and
$x \mapsto e^{-\Lambda(t)} \cdot e^{\,t X(x)}$ are equal, i.e.\ the tilted exponential
factors as the constant $e^{-\Lambda(t)}$ times $e^{\,tX}$.
